Subject: Fine-grained carveouts for OSS & model-output — defense control proposal

Hi Eliot / Finegrain procurement team —

Thanks for the redline and the quick review. Attached is our latest proposed Order Form redline (FG_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf) and an evidence checklist we typically ask for when IP issues are flagged (FG_Evidence_Checklist.xlsx). High-level proposal from our side to try to bridge the gap on indemnity:

- Defense control: Redwood proposes right to assume defense for third-party IP claims that are solely tied to our Hosted models and service runtime; however, we accept a joint-counsel obligation for complex matters and will keep the customer updated.
- OSS & third-party model carveouts: we need explicit carveouts for claims arising solely from open-source components and third-party models that Finegrain brings or authorizes (including downstream fine-tuning that uses customer-supplied models). We propose a defined list and a short notice process to enable triage.
- Notice & cure: customer must provide prompt written notice (we suggest 30 days) and allow Redwood a reasonable cure period (we propose 90 days for remediation or mitigation steps for technical fixes).
- Evidence & cooperation: proposed evidence checklist clarifies what we need (example logs, sample prompts, dataset snapshots).
- Cap & remedies: to get closer to your request for reimbursement, we can agree to a narrowly scoped indemnity limited to direct damages from a covered claim and a mutual cooperation clause; insurance/escrow offsets should apply.

If this looks like a good baseline, can we schedule a 30-minute call with legal + procurement to walk through the redline tomorrow or Wednesday?

Thanks,
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the checklist. A few immediate items from procurement/legal at Finegrain:

1) We cannot accept an unfettered "right to defend" on Redwood's side for claims tied to model output. Our customers require the option to control defense decision-making for claims that impact their business.
2) OSS carveouts are reasonable in principle, but we need clear objective rules for what counts as "OSS" (license list, manifest, SHA of dependencies).
3) Rather than a long cure window, procurement prefers a capped reimbursement route plus a shorter cure period (30 days) so our customers can move quickly.

I've attached a short procurement checklist (not included here) and would like to set a call — are you available Wed 10am PT?

—Eliot

Eliot / team —

Thank you — I reviewed Ben's redline and Frode from our product/ops chimed in on the technical feasibility of evidence requests. To help procurement reconcile the positions, below are redline-ready suggestions (legal rationale included inline in the PDF but summarized here):

- Definition: "Open Source Component" should be an explicitly defined term: OSS component means software with an OSI-approved license listed in an agreed manifest attached to the Order Form. An explicit "Provided Model" carveout (models provided by customer or third parties and not on Redwood's vetted catalog) should also be defined.
- Scope of indemnity: Redwood will indemnify for third-party IP infringement claims solely to the extent such claims arise from Redwood's modifications to non-OSS, Redwood-provided models or our hosted inference stack. Claims arising exclusively from customer-provided models, model prompts or OSS components are excluded. This preserves a reasonable boundary while protecting Finegrain for core Redwood-owned infra/model defects.
- Defense control compromise: Redwood may assume defense with lead counsel, provided Finegrain has the right to select independent counsel at its own expense and to participate. For high-value claims (> $2M), require mutual agreement to Redwood leading defense; absent agreement, the parties share coordination responsibilities and Redwood will advance defense costs subject to insurance/escrow offsets.
- Notice & cure: 30 days' notice is acceptable for most claims; we propose a tiered cure — 30 days for operational fixes, 90 days for technical remediation requiring model retraining or redeployment. If cure is impossible (as documented), we revert to damages/settlement path.
- Evidence & data requests: limit scope to what's strictly necessary — sample prompts, relevant logs, limited dataset excerpts. Any PII or customer-sensitive content will be redacted per our DLP procedures.

I'll attach a marked-up clause set in FG_OrderForm_Redline_v3.pdf and the evidence checklist. From a commercial perspective, Ben — we need procurement to confirm whether the proposed $2M threshold and insurance offsets are workable; if they won't accept that, we should prioritize a short call with Finance to trade off cap vs. carveouts.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Eliot / team —

Thanks for the feedback and Kimberly for the legal markup. To keep momentum on the deal, proposed commercial compromise below:

- Redwood will assume defense for covered third-party IP claims with the following guardrails: Finegrain may appoint independent counsel at its own cost; Redwood will step in with lead counsel but must provide weekly updates and a remediation plan within 10 business days. If Redwood does not pursue a diligent defense plan within that period, Finegrain may take over defense and Redwood will reimburse reasonable documented defense costs up to any agreed insurance/escrow offsets.
- OSS & Provided Model carveouts as Kimberly drafted — objective manifest attachment required at signature.
- Notice & cure: accept two-tier approach (30 days operational, 90 days technical), but Redwood will provide an interim mitigation plan within 5 business days of notice.
- Cap/insurance: propose $2M threshold for Redwood to lead defense without joint approval; above that, mutual sign-off required. Insurance offsets and escrow application as documented in the redline.

Can we lock a 30-minute call Monday 10:00am PT (I'll invite Kimberly + Jordan + Marissa + your procurement lead)? If that works I'll share an updated redline with the guardrail language highlighted.

Ben
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
